entries.title: Remaining leads from the survey of comparable agent orchestrators (Oct 2026)
entries.body:
Leads borrowed from comparable open-source agent orchestrators, surveyed in October 2026 (first imported from issue #671).
Nothing here is a commitment; these are leads to triage.
The orch checked each against the code on 2026-11-17: ideas lym has built or that proved moot are dropped,
partly built ones name only what is still open, and the eight most worth doing are notes of their own in this project.
Each bullet names its source project and the lym module it would touch.

## Plan validation and concurrency (quarry, Plan-Write, board)

- **Typed scope operations on cards** (foremerge): each scope carries an additive or breaking operation,
  and deterministic rules flag colliding pairs even when files do not overlap.
  Worth comparing against board labels and the alignment gate.
- **Symbol leases between concurrent tasks** (Fusion, ORCH): expiring leases on symbol keys serialize overlapping tasks,
  with a deterministic tie-break; lym keeps overlapping tasks apart by board labels.
- **Commit-time reservation guard** (ntm): a pre-commit hook refuses a commit touching what another task holds; needs leases first.
- **Criterion amendment ledger** (oh-my-claudecode): a card's acceptance text changes only through a recorded amendment in weft.

## Review (burler, Bouncer)

- **Quorum of differently-angled judges** (ccswarm): lym fans out lenses but has no quorum vote for high-risk segments.
  Since 2026-11-19 a run's parent orch can be asked to see and veto each Code-Review round and each drift judge ruling
  (`code_review_ask_parent`, `judge_ask_parent`); that is one extra judge, not a quorum.
- **Risk tier by changed paths** (yylo): globs over sensitive paths choose the review depth and the gate scope.

## Engine, recipes and governance (shed, tender, orch, board)

- **Cross-run quarantine** (Bernstein): a task that fails three times across runs is held, unless the failures were the host's.
- **Fork a run from a step with a tree snapshot** (Bernstein): `shed goto` moves the cursor but does not restore the warp tree.
- **Warm retry guarded by a workspace hash** (Bernstein): resume the native session only when the tree is unchanged.
- **Evidence reuse by input identity** (yylo): verify is skipped on the same tree; a changed review prompt could rerun only the review.
- **Guidance at the next step boundary** (Conductor): a queue of operator guidance for the next producer's prompt.
  Partly met since 2026-11-19: `notify_parent_on` in `loom.yaml` mails the run's parent when a named row is reached,
  so the parent can brief that row's agent as it starts; there is still no queue of guidance lym itself folds into the prompt.
- **Batched operator questions with recorded assumptions** (Spec Kit `/clarify`, Conductor): Discussion-Write asks at most a few ranked questions,
  each with a recommended answer, and records unanswered ones as assumptions.
  Since 2026-11-19 a run's autonomous agents put their questions to the run's parent orch, not to the operator in their pane.
  Discussion asks in its pane only when `discussion_interactive` is `true`, which is off by default and forced off by autonomy mode (`30ed1ee58`),
  so this lead concerns an interactive Discussion only.
- **Rate-limit wait**: the orch watcher wakes the orch after a usage reset; tender itself schedules no resume.
- **Standing goals and scheduled routines** (ORCH, CAO, Fusion): periodic triage, dependency bumps or `selfreport` sweeps.

## Agent sessions (reed, shuttle)

- **Waiting-for-input signal** (agent-of-empires): shuttle has an awaiting-input state; screen heuristics still decide readiness and startup.
- **Reference status patterns and a paste pitfall** (CAO): compare its regexes and its tmux bracketed-paste note with shuttle's readiness and creel inject.
- **Context forecasting** (ntm): the orch cycles its context; Webster's Master and the loom driver do not, and nothing forecasts.
- **Staggered spawns** (ntm): space Webster forks and batten fan-out by learned rate limits.

## Observability (report, weft)

- **Hash-chained run journal** (Bernstein): a hash chain over producer outputs makes an archived run self-verifying.
- **Unverified-completion rate** (Bernstein): a `lym report` view of completions with no test or gate behind them.
- **Commit-to-record links** (AgentNote): weft links to warp by a `Warp-SHA:` trailer; a note or trailer on each warp commit could link back.
- **Run diff** (ccswarm): `lym report` comparing two archived runs' timelines and token use.
- **OpenTelemetry spans per producer** (Conductor).

## Operator attention (orch, dobby, reed)

- **Attention feed with acknowledgement states** (ntm): dobby's wait reminders have no seen, snoozed or acknowledged states.

## Discussion review (Discussion-Write, stencils, pattern)

- **Requirements-quality checklist** (Spec Kit `/checklist`): items with IDs the Discussion-review judge answers one by one.
- **Fixed analysis categories** (Kiro): inconsistency, ambiguity, conflicts, unstated assumptions and missing edge cases as named lenses.
- **PATTERN rules handed to reviewers** (Spec Kit constitution): its rules as numbered MUSTs in plan and code review prompts.
- **Glob-scoped steering** (Kiro): stencils pull per-area guidance chosen by the paths of a plan's glyphs.

entries.title: A closed area for lym: bwrap sandbox in stages, off by default
entries.brief: Run the lym process tree in a bwrap area with a host proxy and broker, built in three stages with a stop; to be split if it goes ahead
entries.body:
## Seen (operator, 2026-10-30)

Every agent lym starts runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, which many people do not accept, and a repository that states it supports safe sandboxing is worth more than one that does not.
The area matters most on the work machine OSL-1046 (operator, 2026-11-22).
On OSL-1046 sudo is tightly limited and does not cover AppArmor, so the profile `bwrap` needs on Ubuntu 24.04 cannot be loaded there; a `bwrap` area, and podman or Claude Code's `/sandbox`, which need the same user namespaces, are blocked on that machine until IT loads it. Landlock needs no privilege and is the option left to weigh there.
The operator uses lym alone, on Linux (OSL-1046: Ubuntu 24.04; Neve: Kubuntu on Ubuntu 26.04, Plasma 6), and has no interest in other users or in Windows.
The research is `docs/research/platform/sandboxing-options-2026-10-30.md`: it weighs `bwrap`, Landlock, a dedicated Linux user, systemd sandboxing, podman and Claude Code's own `/sandbox`, and the packages and cards each would change.

Two exposures hold today with no area: an agent can reach `/run/user/<uid>/bus` and through it `systemd-run --user`, which starts any process outside lym's tree, and it can type into other hubs' tmux panes through their sockets in `/tmp/tmux-<uid>`, the Models hub's among them.

## Idea

Run the whole lym process tree inside a `bwrap` area launched by lym itself, with the agents free inside it and a short, controlled list of exits.
It is an option the operator turns on, never a requirement: with it off, everything works as it does today, and with it on, nothing starts when the sandbox cannot.
The operator thinks the full design is complicated and error-prone, and doubts it will work without large problems, so it is built in stages with a stop between them.
This is one large note and is split into tasks, or a project, only when the operator decides it goes ahead.

### Before the area: two cheap steps

- Start a hub's tmux server from a Konsole window, not a VS Code terminal: the server inherits the `vscode` AppArmor profile, which grants user namespaces to every agent of the hub.
- A line in `README.md` that every agent lym starts runs with bypass permissions, and that lym belongs on a machine the operator is willing to hand to its agents.

### Stage 1: the filesystem area only

`bwrap` with `--unshare-all --die-with-parent --clearenv` around reed's tmux server and everything under it, started by a new `lym area start` and a supervisor inside.

- The hub is bound read-write at its own path, since the tmux server name, the creel socket name, git's worktree links and Claude Code's transcript directory all derive from absolute paths; `/usr`, `/etc` and `/opt` are read-only, `$HOME` a tmpfs with read-only binds of the Go toolchain, the Claude Code binary and the installed `lym`.
- The area has its own Claude config directory and Go caches bound at the usual paths, with the host's plugin cache read-only on top, so the host's `settings.json` hooks never run in it.
- One host directory holds the tmux socket directory, so `lym reed attach` from outside drives the server inside; tried on OSL-1046 with a tmux server inside `bwrap`.
- `.git/hooks` is read-only; `.git/config` was to stay writable for `branch.<b>.lymLocal`, but `fabric-remote-async` removed that mark and `internal/gitrepo/branchmark.go`, so the reason is gone; whether git itself or another lym writer still needs `.git/config` writable is unchecked.
- Network stays open and there is no broker, so the landing deploy, `lym reed window`, `lym ide` and `lym hibernate request` do not work from inside; the operator does them by hand, from outside.
- A config module `area` with `required`, off by default; `lym area start` refuses on any failure and never falls back to an unsandboxed start.
- Ubuntu 24.04 needs a one-time AppArmor profile for `/usr/bin/bwrap`, loaded by root; the report names the profile, and Ubuntu 25.04 and later ship it, which is not verified on Neve.

This closes the two exposures above and shows early whether tmux, creel and dobby run well inside an area.

### Stop: the operator decides whether stage 1 works well enough to go on.

### Stage 2: egress through a host proxy

No network inside the area; a host-side proxy, reached through a bound socket, allows CONNECT to `api.anthropic.com`, `claude.ai`, `platform.claude.com`, `proxy.golang.org`, `sum.golang.org`, `github.com` and `api.github.com`, with a loopback relay inside the area.
Telemetry and the auto-updater are off by environment.
The GitHub token handed to the area is fine-grained and limited to the hub's repositories; the operator's `gh` login never enters.
WebFetch and the `prowler` skill reach only these hosts.

### Stage 3: a broker for the remaining exits

A host-side process serving a fixed set of verbs and never a command line from the area: the landing deploy (it fetches `origin/main` into its own clone, checks the commit is the tip, builds with the host's Go and installs), `lym reed window` opening Konsole, and `lym hibernate request`.
`lym ide` is refused, since VS Code on the host would run git over repositories the area writes; the host runs no git over the area's repositories at all.

## What is not claimed

Isolation from a kernel exploit, which needs a virtual machine; that data in the area cannot leave through an allowed host; and that a landed change of lym itself cannot run on the host once deployed, which matters on this hub because it develops lym.
Landlock stays a possible inner layer once both machines run a kernel with ABI 9 and 10, and Claude Code deny rules in shuttle's settings are a cheap second line inside the area; the dedicated user, podman, systemd sandboxing and Claude Code's `/sandbox` inside lym runs are left out.
The report estimates the whole at five tasks and eighteen cards.

## Related

Note `creel-cross-hub-mail`: the inbox folder sits outside an area, so reading and writing it goes through the broker.

entries.title: Measure what Cortex XDR costs the test suites on OSL-1046
entries.brief: The 242 s fabricengine tier 1 against 37 to 41 s elsewhere is a machine difference no report has split
entries.body:
## Seen (operator, 2026-11-09)

Cortex XDR on OSL-1046 holds each new binary for about 10 s and scans each file a test creates, and fabricengine tests create many.
The shard report (`docs/research/speed/fabricengine-shards-2026-11-09/report.md`) put the 242 s one-process wall down to load, but the 2026-11-08 figure of 37 to 41 s was measured on another machine, so the gap is machine and Cortex, not load.
The package used 1.23 cores of 16 and `pmd` and `piud` were busy in nearly every sample.

## Idea

Separate the Cortex cost from the rest: the time a freshly built test binary waits before it runs, the time file creation takes with and without a scanned folder, and the fabricengine tier 1 wall with the repository and temp folders excluded from the scan, if the operator can have that changed.
The result says whether to cut tests, cut file and binary creation, or ask for an exclusion.

entries.title: Study whether the hardener finds and fixes real faults
entries.brief: Judge the two fabric hardener campaigns from their records: real findings, sound fixes, focus kept, cost
entries.body:
## Goal

Find out whether the hardener recipe does what it is for: drive the modules its focus names, find real faults, fix them with tests that hold, and converge.

## Evidence

- The first fabric campaign, `harden-fabricengine`, landed as `37649c772` after three rounds.
- The second, `harden-fabric-single-repo-verbs`, the one-repository fabric campaign with the fabric verbs in its sandbox, has landed as `2722a66ef`, so both campaigns are judged.
- The second campaign ran with the model rotation the template then set (opus, fable, sonnet).
  Hardener rounds now default to `sonnet[high]` alone, and a rotation is set per run through `hardener.reviewer` and `hardener.fixer` (`a66d41345`), so judge the rotation's cost and effect against that change.
- The five faults the second campaign found but could not raise were the task `harden-fabric-undriven-cases`, which has landed as `540e8c9b5`.
  Judge that fix as the campaign's follow-through.
- Each campaign's round files are under its records worktree at `_lym/reviews/harden/`: `round-<n>-focus.md`, `round-<n>-review.md`, `round-<n>-acceptance.md`, `round-<n>-usage.yaml` and the snapshots, beside its decision record and the landed commits.

## Questions

- **Findings**: for each finding, is it a real fault, a false positive or a matter of taste? Do its repro steps show it?
- **Fixes**: does each fix cure its finding? Does its regression test fail with the fix broken, as the fix rules demand? Was the package doc updated?
- **Focus**: did each round stay inside the campaign's focus? Did the focus files steer later rounds to what was left unverified?
- **Convergence**: did the Bouncer end the campaign on a sound verdict? Were deferred findings filed as open risks and on the board?
- **Misses**: which faults in the same code turned up after the campaign landed, outside it (such as the killed-seed way forward in `0e4782373` and the fetch prune in `f660ac101`), and could the campaign have reached them?
- **Cost**: tokens and wall time per round, from the usage files and the run's records.
- **Seen in the second campaign**: round 2's reviewer recorded smaller faults (O1 to O6) only as prose, since an incremental round admits only BLOCKING findings on changed hunks.
  Round 3's reviewer (sonnet, medium, 4 min) approved with half its focus undriven: the killed discard, the keep-local tag push, a failed step with no kill, and `adopt --archives` over real owner tags.
  A settled harden segment cannot be reopened (`lym loom goto` refuses), so the orch had no way to order another round. Judge each of these, and whether the remaining focus should block approval.
  Round 4 again raised what it found outside the incremental scope only as prose; those are the O1 to O5 that `harden-fabric-undriven-cases` fixed.
  A suspected cause is the stencils, not the model: `contracts/stencils/harden/harden-rubric-review.md` asks for OK, WARN or FAIL on every focus entry,
  while `contracts/stencils/burler/burler-review-format.md` lets an incremental round raise only BLOCKING findings on changed hunks, so such a round can only approve. Judge that conflict.
  Since `8cf7f4775`, a later hardener round cannot approve with its focus undriven:
  the reviewer raises a `decision`-class, BLOCKING, `origin: focus` finding for each focus entry it left undriven or marked WARN,
  `burlerengine.CheckReviewRound` exempts it from the changed-file rule, and the arbiter and then the parent rule on it.
  That answers whether the remaining focus should block approval going forward; judge the campaign's rounds as they ran, and whether the new finding is enough for the rubric conflict.

## Bounds

- Mostly a study of records and commits.
- At most three findings are reproduced, on a sandbox hub against the commit before their fix, one try each; no other trial runs.
- The report ends with a verdict and a short list of concrete changes to the hardener recipe or its stencils, each a candidate note.

entries.title: Bouncer escalation fixes: fixed BLOCKING findings, soft-cap accept, auto-accept flag, untested wiring
entries.body:
## fixed-blocking-escalates-parent

### Seen

Since `code-bouncer-asks-parent` landed (8cf7f4775), four darn runs on 2026-11-23 stopped at Code-Bouncer with cause `budget` after round 1:
`amend-plan-loses-webster-batches`, `pr-findings-open-fabric-nil`, `beam-pr-describes-itself` and `godocreflow-worsens-findings`.
In each, the fixer had fixed every finding, BLOCKING included, committed it and passed its gates;
the ledger still held the BLOCKING entry `open`, because no later round re-reviewed the fix, and a darn's budget is spent after one round.
The orch then read the fixer report and the commit and accepted each time, which cost each run a parent turn and a wait.

### Idea

A BLOCKING finding the fixer reports `fixed`, with a commit and a green gate, is verified without a full review round before the Bouncer judges the budget:
for example, a short verification of only those findings against the fix commit, which closes the entry or keeps it open.
The parent is asked only when a BLOCKING finding stays open after that check, or the fixer did not fix it.

## below-window-accept-blocking

Left open when `code-bouncer-asks-parent` landed (8cf7f4775), as finding `below-window-decision-accept-passes-open-blocking`.

A decision accept recorded below the soft-cap window passes over an open BLOCKING ledger entry of another class, in `internal/shedadapters/bouncerdecision.go`.
That lets a run land past an open BLOCKING finding, which the landed task was meant to stop: the run should ask the parent instead.

## budget-escalation-untested

Left open when `code-bouncer-asks-parent` landed (8cf7f4775), as finding `budget-escalation-decision-detail-unasserted`.

The decision-findings detail appended to a budget escalation has no test asserting it, in `internal/shedadapters/bouncer_escalation_test.go`.

## code-auto-accept-flag-only

Left open when `code-bouncer-asks-parent` landed (8cf7f4775), as finding `code-auto-accept-meaning-change-no-reinterpretation`.

The narrowed meaning of `code_auto_accept` reaches hubs only through a flagging reinterpretation in `internal/loomengine/reinterpret.go`, with no rewrite.
Confirm a flag is enough, or rewrite the hub layers that set the key.

## hardener-focus-wiring-untested

Left open when `code-bouncer-asks-parent` landed (8cf7f4775), as finding `hardener-focus-permission-wiring-untested`.

The wiring that lets a hardener round raise a focus finding (`FocusFindings` into the round context) is not covered end to end, in `internal/burlercli` and `internal/shedadapters/roundcontext.go`.

entries.title: Parent-review asks look up the orch pane in a stale tmux window, so an approved PR review cannot end
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #206](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/206).

Seen in hub mo, beam dop-support-3, run hydraulics-gaps, at PR-Review with pr_review_ask_parent on. The parent orch strand mo:dop-support-3:orch is live at pane %10 in window @8, but lym loom parent-review ask records each ask from the PR-Review session as no-parent, apparently looking for the orch in window @4. The asks the row itself sends at a new head are delivered: asks 3 and 7 were answered. lym loom parent-review answer then refuses a no-parent ask ('ask 9 is already no-parent; ... wait for the next [pr-review request]'), and lym loom pr-continue refuses with 'no satisfied answer from your parent stands at <head>'. Once the parent is satisfied at an unchanged head, the review therefore cannot end. Workaround: turn pr_review_ask_parent off for the run with lym config loom --layer local --set pr_review_ask_parent=false in the task worktree, then have the PR-Review agent run pr-continue. Expected: the ask resolves the orch's current pane, and a parent can answer, or record a satisfied verdict for, the head that a no-parent ask named. Related: #200.

entries.title: Webster stops after an amended plan send the parent no notice, and webster reset leaves the run tied to the dropped code tip
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #207](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/207).

## What happened

Run `models-torque-drag-adapter` (tapestry, under autonomy) went `blocked` at Webster after a parent decision with `--amends-plan` and a replan.
`lym loom status` gave:

> webster: the auto-rebaseline of the changed plan blocks this run: webster: the edited plan changes the cards of a batch this run already begun: 00-overview.md changed outside its Card Index; ...

The parent orch got no creel mail for this stop.
Its last mail from the run was the arbiter's "settled the review escalation at Plan-Bouncer and resumed the run" (12:21 UTC); the block came later, and only the operator noticed it.
Every other stop of the same run (question stops, batten failures) was mailed by `dop:LOOM` or `dop:BATTEN`.

## Two defects

1. A Webster auto-rebaseline block sends no stop notice to the run's parent. Under autonomy the orch must hear of every stop, so this one stalls the run silently.
2. The Plan rows that apply an `--amends-plan` decision edit `00-overview.md` outside its Card Index (here, the plan's opening summary) even when batches have already begun, and the plan gate accepts that, but Webster's rebaseline then refuses it. The plan rows should keep to the Card Index after a begun batch, or Plan's gate should refuse the edit, so the two agree.

3. After that, the run blocked again because batch 03 was dead from before the amendment. It named `lym webster reset --to batch-start --batch 03` as the way forward.
   That reset moved the code branch and origin back to e1ab782 and committed `webster: reset` to the records with `Warp-SHA` but no `Run-Transition` trailer.
   The run's last transition still named the dropped tip 9fff222, so `lym loom resume` refused ("the code tip 9fff222 the run's last transition names is not on origin yet"), and `lym loom goto --to Webster` wrote no transition either.
   Past `runfsm.CodeTipGrace` the dobby would have returned the run to its previous transition.
   `webster reset` (and `goto`) should commit a transition naming the new tip.
   None of these stops sent the parent a notice either.

## Fix applied by hand

The orch restored the summary paragraph in `00-overview.md`, kept the Card Index line, committed it, and ran `lym loom resume`.
After the reset it committed an empty records commit carrying `Warp-SHA: e1ab782…` and `Run-Transition: models-torque-drag-adapter`, pushed it, and ran `lym loom resume`; Webster then ran.

entries.title: PR-Review row does not notice its session ended
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #210](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/210).

Seen in hub mo, run hydraulics-gaps, PR-Review row. The PR-Review session's strand was removed (lym reed remove) at 13:44, and the session logged SessionEnd. The row's lym loom step process went on running with status running at PR-Review, and spawned no new session, until the process was killed by hand at 13:50. Only then did the run mark the row interrupted, and a resume start a fresh session. Expected: the row detects a dead PR-Review session and re-spawns it under the interrupt policy, or halts with a stop the parent can act on.

entries.title: Red-first gate must support C# repositories
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #208](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/208).

The red-first gate runs the diff's new tests on the merge base only through the Go scoper. In a C# repository (NORCE Models, a .NET solution tested with NUnit) it cannot select or run those tests, and it halts every writer's handoff until the parent records a 'No test seam' waiver by hand. The gate never runs there, so a C# run gets no red-first protection at all.

Expected: the gate supports C# as a first-class language.
- Select the tests the diff adds or changes, by test project and fully qualified name (dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~...), from the changed *.cs files under test projects.
- Build and run them on the merge base in a scratch checkout, through the hub's own C# test command or tier configuration, and judge red on the merge base and green at the head as for Go.
- Treat a test that does not compile on the merge base, because it reads a member the change adds, as red with that reason, not as a missing seam.
- Halt only when the selection or build fails for a reason the writer can act on.

Related: #192, which reports the halt itself.

entries.title: A killed batten cancel leaves a remove record whose way forward fails once the pair is gone
entries.brief: The record names lym fabric remove --remote, which answers pair not found; batten cancel --remove is the re-run that works
entries.body:
## Seen

Live drive of the one-repository sandbox (`docs/research/single-repo-undriven-cases.md`).
`lym batten cancel <slug> --remove`, killed while its detached `lym fabric remote-teardown` child stalled on an origin branch delete,
leaves a pending record of kind `remove`.
`lym fabric status` lists it with the way forward `... run \`lym fabric remove <slug> --remote\` again`.
Run once the pair was gone, that command answers `{"error":"pair not found: nothing of \"disc1\" remains","ok":false}`.
The command that finished the teardown was `lym batten cancel <slug> --remove`.

## Idea

When the record's pair is gone, or the record came from a batten cancel, name `lym batten cancel <slug> --remove` as the re-run,
the way the `discard` record's `rerun` field already does.

entries.title: Autonomy: a failed later ask hides the parent's satisfied answer, and the parent cannot settle it
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #213](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/213).

Import note: the issue names files under `.lym/`, which is deleted with its worktree, so only what the issue quotes of them reached the board: `.lym/parent-review/asks.json`.

## Seen

Under autonomy, PR-Review deadlocked twice on 2026-11-23, in `hydraulics-gaps` and `steady-wob-nan-at-zero-rotation`.
708cdadc5 fixes the first link: the PR-Review agent's own `parent-review ask` is now delivered, and a refused post ends `undelivered` rather than `no-parent`.
The links below remain.

In `steady-wob-nan-at-zero-rotation`'s `.lym/parent-review/asks.json`:

- Ask 2 is the row's own ask at head 038cf197. The orch answered it `--satisfied`, and it is `done`.
- Asks 3 and 4 were sent from the agent's pane at the same head and did not reach the orch.
- `lym loom pr-continue` then refused with "no satisfied answer from your parent stands at 038cf197; ask your parent again with lym loom parent-review ask".

## Still open

1. `pr-continue` judges by the latest ask at the head.
   A later ask that did not reach the parent hides a satisfied answer the parent already gave at the same head.
   Any failed later ask now does this, including `undelivered` and `timeout`.
2. The parent has no verb to settle an ask it never received.
   `parent-review answer` refuses a `no-parent` ask, and presumably an `undelivered` one too, and `parent-review ask` refuses any caller but the PR-Review session.
   Once the agent's asks keep failing, only a hand edit of `"autonomy": false` in the weft's `_lym/shed/<slug>/pull-request.json` lets `pr-continue` pass.
3. 708cdadc5 notes that no test runs the ask from a real creel pane, so the strand claim creel accepts from a live PR-Review pane is unproven.

## Idea

- Let `pr-continue` pass when a satisfied parent answer stands at the current head, whatever the state of later asks at that head.
- Let the parent record a satisfied answer at the current head without a delivered ask, for example `lym loom parent-review answer <slug> --head <sha> --satisfied`.
- Add a test that runs the ask verb from a live non-orch pane.

Related: #200, #206, #211.

entries.title: Reed's Slack button click leaves forwarding off with no trace
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #212](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/212).

On the prime's reed session, clicking the slack toggle in the status bar left `lym slack status` at forwarding [] and relay_live false, and showed nothing on the bar. No trace log of a `slack toggle` run was written. Running the same command by hand from the prime anchor, `lym slack toggle slack --socket <reed socket> --tmux /usr/bin/tmux --client /dev/pts/15`, turned forwarding on for mo:orch, started the relay and made the channel at once. The session's @lym_button_dir and @lym_orch_dir both name the prime anchor. The toggle command in @lym_slack_toggle_command sends stdout and stderr to /dev/null, so a failure before the bar redraw leaves no sign. Expected: a click flips the button, or the bar or a log shows why it did not.

## Issue comment, 2026-11-23

Likely related: bc5799ced (2026-11-17) moved the Slack toggle to the orch's session only, read through the new `@lym_orch_dir`, and its description lists a real tmux Slack click as not run by hand. The relay's last healthy time before this was 2026-11-12, so no click had been made on the new toggle until now. In a task session the bar draws the away toggle alone, and away does nothing while the relay is down.
